---
title: "Electrostatics"
description: "Colour a molecular surface by an electrostatic potential from APBS."
execute:
  daemon: false
---

[APBS](https://www.poissonboltzmann.org/) solves the Poisson-Boltzmann equation for a molecule in solvent and writes the electrostatic potential on a grid, usually as a `.dx` file. Its values are in kT/e: thermal energy per elementary charge, about 25.7 mV at 25 °C.

This example uses the potential of one barnase-barstar pair from [1BRS](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1BRS) (barnase chain A, barstar chain D), made with pdb2pqr and APBS by `docs/dev/apbs_1brs.py`. Barnase is positively charged and barstar negatively charged.

```{python}
import molecularnodes as mn
from molecularnodes.nodes import geometry as mg

canvas = mn.Canvas()
```

## Load the potential

Load the grid as a density and show it with `Density Style ISO Surface`, which meshes the potential at +1 kT/e (blue) and -1 kT/e (red).

```{python}
esp = mn.entities.density.Grids.load("../../tests/data/1brs_AD_apbs.dx.gz")

with esp.tree.reset(input="Volume") as (volume, join):
    (
        volume
        >> mg.DensityStyleISOSurface(
            threshold=1.0,
            positive_color=(0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 1.0),
            negative_color=(1.0, 0.1, 0.1, 1.0),
            material=mn.material.Transparent(
                transparency=0.7, fresnel=True, outline_color=(0.85, 0.85, 0.85, 1.0)
            ).material,
        )
        >> join
    )
```

## Colour the surface

Passing the density as `color` samples the potential at every vertex of the surface, from -5 kT/e (red) to 5 kT/e (blue). The density keeps its source volume in the `MN/Volume` bundle of its styled output, so it can be sampled while it shows its own style. The coordinates of 1BRS line up with the grid because pdb2pqr keeps the input coordinates.

```{python}
mol = mn.Molecule.fetch("1BRS")
mol.add_style("surface", selection="chainID A D", color=esp)
```

```{python}
canvas.look_at(esp, viewpoint=(106.5, 0.0, -37.7))
canvas.snapshot()
```

Hide the potential's own style to see only the coloured surface. Barnase (left) is mostly positive and barstar (right) mostly negative.

```{python}
esp.object.hide_render = True
canvas.look_at(mol, viewpoint=(106.5, 0.0, -37.7))
canvas.snapshot()
```

The colour range is set on the `Color Sample Grid` node in the molecule's tree, through its `Min` and `Max` inputs.
